description:  This project is dedicated to collecting high-quality macOS software and organizing them systematically by different categories for easy search and use.

summary.one_liner: A curated, categorized list of macOS applications, with each entry tagged for open-source status, freeware, App Store availability, and native-app status.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome" link list rather than software: it collects macOS apps and sorts them into categories such as text editors, office suites, note-taking, PDF tools, developer utilities, API clients, and network analysis. Each entry is a one-line description with icons marking open source, free, App Store, and native status. The README's table of contents shows the full category tree, including sections for AI tools, communication, security, utilities, and gaming. Several contributor-promoted apps are listed at the top as sponsors, which are excluded from this summary. The visible portion of the README ends partway through the Developer Tools section, so later categories are not verified here.
use_cases: find a macOS app for a specific task
compare open-source and free Mac editors
discover Markdown or note-taking apps for Mac
find API clients, proxies, or hex editors on macOS
locate PDF, ebook, or RSS reader apps for Mac
browse developer tools and IDEs for Mac
notable: Entries are tagged with icons for open source, freeware, App Store, native app, and linked awesome lists
Organized into a deep category tree with subcategories for developer tools and utilities
Accepts community pull requests and links to contributing guidelines
Includes translated versions of the README in Chinese, Korean, and Japanese
Includes a separate section on genuine download sites and a blocklist of pirated software sites
caveats: Lists third-party apps only; the list itself does not provide software to install
The visible README is truncated, so the full list of categories and entries is not verified here
Some entries are commercial or subscription products, and freeness is not always stated
